quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: WHAT EPC POWER ACTUALLY BRINGS (Chris, CTO/Chief Strategy Officer of SpinCo): EPC 'really is covering a gap that we had that was kind of upstream in the data center.' Its base product is not a normal energy-storage box but 'a grid-forming inverter' that (1) insulates the utility grid from 'some of the anomalies that happen in a GPU-based data center, some of those power fluctuations' and (2) delivers 'a very clean source of power to the IT loads in the data center' - a capability 'being required by a lot of utilities here across the U.S.' The forward technology content is the bigger prize: 'They have a centralized rectifier today, an active digital rectifier that we can use for centralized 800-volt DC deployments. This is already in the NVIDIA DGX architecture. They have a very far along SST development program that will allow us to even bolster efficiency better and improve the footprint.' The stated ambition: 'we are going to be taking the data center architecture to a blank sheet of paper soon and being able to work with customers on really helping them connect that 34.5 kV at the utility space directly to the IT load.'
quarterly_data.figure: centralized 800-volt DC deployments; connect 34.5 kV at the utility space directly to the IT load

quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: EPC'S 2027 IS ALREADY BOOKED, AND A JULY GRID EVENT IS PULLING DEMAND FORWARD (Chris): asked what drives EPC's growth, 'It is all pinned to the data centers. It is all pinned to some of those regulatory requirements that are coming. There is also some tailwinds from bans on foreign-produced product in the critical infrastructure here in the U.S. EPC is all U.S.-based production, so that plays in very well.' Asked about visibility: 'Most of that business is booked today' and 'Really good backlog for 2027.' A specific catalyst was named: 'There was a pretty significant power disturbance in Northern Virginia back in the month of July, and that is driving more utilities to demand this type of technology in the data center.' Margin uplift is attributed to capacity that 'just came online in the month of June', supply-chain reshoring initiatives, and the fact that 'data center margins are a little bit higher than what their traditional business has been.'

quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FLEX'S OWN HIGH-VOLTAGE PRODUCT IS SHIPPING INTO EXISTING DATA CENTERS; EPC IS THE GREENFIELD PLAY (Chris): 'If you look at where Flex's primary power conversion business has been, it has all been really at the rack or near the rack... we have a pretty broad portfolio of product that allow us to take, whether it be AC power or even 800-volt DC power, all the way down to one volt, which is the voltage level that these chips operate. We are deploying both plus/minus 400 and 800-volt DC sidecars as well. And those are being implemented in data centers that are already built today or in the process of being built. So we see a next two to three years really strong outlook for that type of product.' EPC sits one step upstream and one cycle later: 'Where we see the EPC product playing more of a role is in that greenfield data center that is probably in the planning stages today, and two to three years from now, we will start seeing a lot of demand for their 800-volt DC solutions.'
quarterly_data.figure: plus/minus 400 and 800-volt DC sidecars deploying now; 800-volt DC greenfield demand two to three years from now

quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: THE POWER-DENSITY MATH BEHIND THE DEMAND CALL (Chris): NIMBY/siting pushback is not seen changing the trajectory - 'I do not think we are going to see demand curtail in the data center space, even with some of these back pressures. It may just shift around a little bit' - because the driver is silicon power: 'you are taking chips that used to operate at 150 watts are now going to 3,000 watts. It is a 20-fold increase in power. There is not a growth estimate out there that is not below two to three times the amount of power consumption in the data center fleet here in the U.S.' Flex is spending against it: 'We are making those investments in capacity to make sure that we can meet those demands.' On procurement, the CFO said the component environment 'is challenged, but it has been challenged for a while... for the better part of 7 years', and that the 65% to 75% CPI growth guide 'contemplated supply challenges in there.'
quarterly_data.figure: chips from 150 watts to 3,000 watts, a 20-fold increase in power; two to three times the amount of power consumption in the data center fleet here in the U.S.

quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: WHAT STAYS WITH REMAINCO FLEX AFTER THE SPIN - THE ENERGY-INFRASTRUCTURE CONTRACT MANUFACTURING (Michael, CEO of RemainCo Flex): 'This is a business that we spun the power product portfolio into SpinCo, but we're maintaining all the contract manufacturing business inside of Flex. Whether it's power generation, transmission, distribution, storage, all of that contract manufacturing work stays inside of Flex. Those areas will be positively influenced by the trends in the data center.' The spin is expected 'just after the first of the year', and RMS/ITS margins have gone 'from 5% to 5.7%' over the last two quarters with a long-term target to be set at the November Investor Day. CFO Kevin, separately, said RemainCo will retain a stake in SpinCo that 'will not exceed 19.9%' and expects to use that retained stake to de-lever, leaving Flex 'with less leverage, stronger balance sheet'.
quarterly_data.figure: retained SpinCo stake will not exceed 19.9%; RMS/ITS margins from 5% to 5.7%

quarterly_data.quarter: Flex Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ITS GROWTH IS ALL COMMUNICATIONS, AND SATCOM IS NOW PART OF IT (CFO Kevin): the ITS guide already given on the Q1 FY2027 call was restated - 'In this last earnings, we raised our guidance to high single digits to low double digits. That is really coming on the backs of our communications business,' because 'the lifestyle business is soft as expected. It has been soft for, I want to say, a couple of years now. We do not see a catalyst for that to change anytime soon.' The communications growth is specified as 'that spectrum that is that advanced networking application, high-speed switches, optical gear, network interface technologies, and now SATCOM.' Durability is tied directly to the data center: 'it is as sustainable as the data center demand is sustainable. We believe in that demand. Believed in it so much that we spun the data center business.'
quarterly_data.figure: SATCOM now named inside the advanced-networking spectrum driving ITS growth
